expected.insightNarrative:
Dashboard 1 is the Boston Marathon Data Explorer: every finisher of the Boston Marathon from 1990 to 2025, 663,035 in total, with the field split between men and women, the distribution of finish times, the number of finishers per year and the ten fastest men and women with the weather on their race day. The controls at the top are set to the years 1990 to 2025, all age brackets, both genders, Split Men and Women on, Show Top X at 10 and Temperature Type at Temperature. The story is a race dominated in numbers by men under 40, a field that has more than doubled since 1990, and course records set in 2011 and 2025.

Key insights
- Men under 40 are the largest group of finishers by far: 200,317, or 30.22% of all 663,035 finishers.
- Finish times for men cluster around 3:30 and for women around 3:50 to 4:00, with long tails out to 7:00.
- Men's finishers rose from about 6,500 a year in 1990 to about 16,000 in 2025 and women's from about 2,000 to about 12,000; the 1996 centennial race spiked to nearly 30,000 men, and 2020 shows no finishers.
- The fastest men's times are Geoffrey Mutai's 2:03:02 and Moses Mosop's 2:03:06 in 2011; the fastest women's are Sharon Lokedi's 2:17:22 and Hellen Obiri's 2:17:41 in 2025.

Total
Total finishers: 663,035 for the selected years, age brackets and genders.

Gender Age Pie
The split of finishers by gender and age bracket as a donut: men under 40 are the largest slice at 200,317 finishers (30.22% of the total), followed by men 40 and over, women under 40 and women 40 and over.

Time Distribution
The distribution of finish times from 2:00 to 7:00 as a share of finishers, men in green and women in red: men peak at about 1.3% of finishers just after 3:00 and again near 3:30, women peak at about 1.3% between 3:45 and 4:00, and both curves taper to zero by about 6:30.

Finishers Over Time
Finishers per year from 1990 to 2025: men (green) grow from about 6,500 to about 16,000 and women (red) from about 2,000 to about 12,000, with a spike to nearly 30,000 men in the 1996 centennial race, a jump in 2014, a drop in 2020 when no finishers are recorded, and a dip in 2021 before the recovery.

Top Finishers
The ten fastest men and women with the weather at the start and finish: men led by Geoffrey Mutai (2011, 2:03:02), Moses Mosop (2011, 2:03:06), John Korir (2025, 2:04:45), Gebregziabher Gebremariam (2011, 2:04:53) and Ryan Hall (2011, 2:04:58), then Alphonce Felix Simbu and Cybrian Kotut (2025, 2:05:04), Conner Mantz (2025, 2:05:08), Robert Kiprono Cheruiyot (2010, 2:05:52) and Evans Chebet (2023, 2:05:54); women led by Sharon Lokedi (2025, 2:17:22), Hellen Obiri (2025, 2:17:41), Yalemzerf Yehualaw (2025, 2:18:06), Buzunesh Deba (2014, 2:19:59), Mare Dibaba (2014, 2:20:35), Jemima Jelagat Sumgong (2014, 2:20:41), Margaret Okayo (2002, 2:20:43), Peres Jepchirchir (2022, 2:21:01) and Ababel Yeshaneh (2022, 2:21:05). The 2011 records came on a 46F to 55F day with a 12 mph easterly tailwind; the 2025 times on a 51F to 54F day with a 3 to 8 mph wind from the northwest.
